Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment focuses on site-specific N-glycopeptide analysis of serum haptoglobin using EThcD fragmentation and HILIC enrichment. Label-free quantification was performed using Byologic software.

scope: Haptoglobin was immunopurified from 20 μL of serum in patients with early HCC, liver cirrhosis, and healthy controls, respectively, followed by trypsin/GluC digestion, glycopeptide enrichment, and LC-EThcD-MS/MS analysis.
Haptoglobin (Hp) was purified from 20 μL of patient serum using an antibody-immobilized HPLC column

The immunopurification was performed on a Beckman Coulter HPLC system (Fullerton, CA) with a PEEK column (4.6 mm × 50 mm) packed in-house with the UltraLink hydrazide resin (Thermo Scientific, Rockford, IL) conjugated with an antihuman Hp antibody (Abcam, Cambridge, MA).

evidence: Haptoglobin was immunopurified from 20 μL of serum in patients with early HCC, liver cirrhosis, and healthy controls, respectively
Each sample was analyzed with two injections, and the average normalized abundance of a given N-glycopeptide from the two replicates was used to measure its relative levels between disease groups.

Differential quantitation analysis showed that 5 site-specific N-glycopeptides on sites N184 and N241 were significantly elevated in early HCC compared to cirrhosis (p < 0.05) and normal controls (p ≤ 0.001).
The increased variety of N-glycopeptides in liver diseases compared to healthy controls was due to increased branching with hyper-fucosylation and sialylation.
Five site-specific N-glycopeptides were found to be significantly elevated in early HCC compared to cirrhosis (Table 2), with at least a 2-fold change and p < 0.05.
